newsitem.title: UK: LME plans automatic in-money options declaration.
newsitem.headline: LME plans automatic in-money options declaration.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) Board of Directors adopted an amended recommendation by the traded options committee for the automatic declaration of in-the-money options at its December 13 meeting, the LME said.
The procedure will apply initially to exchange options only, and not client options.
The timing of the new procedures has not been finalised, but the LME said in a notice that it hoped to introduce them around the third quarter of next year.

Under the procedure, on the last trading day of the expiring exchange option the secretariat will calculate the at-the-money strike price and the range of exchange options which will be automatically declared for each metal in each clearing currency.

The Secretariat will identify the at-the-money strike price as being the closest strike price to the futures price for the relevant prompt date, and this will be published as final at the same time as futures valuations are published as being final.
An exchange call option will be declared automatically if it is in-the-money with a strike price that is two gradations or more below the at-the-money strike price.
An exchange put option will be declared automatically if it is in-the-money with a strike price that is two gradations or more above the at-the-money strike price.
All other exchange options will be subject to manual declaration by the taker in accordance with the current procedures, the LME said.

In the event of an excessive overnight price move, under the new procedures the takers of the options will be able to reverse the automatic exercise of an option by manual intervention prior to the time when declarations become effective.

It is the takers' responsibility to ensure any in-the-money exchange options subject to manual declaration are declared, and that out-of-the-money options still subject to automatic declaration as a result of a large price move are manually un-declared, the LME notice said.
The new procedures do not include client options, but it would not be a breach of LME rules for members to adopt the procedure for the declaration of client options, the LME added.
